journal_name: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology

abstracts.abstract: Software verification of concurrent systems remains challenging due to exponential state space explosion. This paper introduces Game-Based Compositional Verification (GBCV), a paradigm-shifting game-theoretic framework that fundamentally reframes verification as strategic interaction between system and environment. We model concurrent software components as players in a两人零和游戏 where verification conditions become game objectives. Our theoretical contribution lies in developing compositional strategies that enable component-wise property verification while preserving system-level guarantees through strategy composition theorems. The framework introduces novel concepts of winning strategies that decompose global verification into local game solutions, achieving exponential complexity reduction compared to explicit-state model checking. We prove that GBCV can handle systems with thousands of concurrent components where traditional approaches become infeasible. The theoretical foundations establish that game-theoretic reasoning provides a more natural and scalable approach to concurrent verification than existing formal methods. This work opens new research directions by connecting software verification with game theory, representing a paradigm shift in how we reason about concurrent software correctness.

Taint analysis serves as a fundamental technique for security vulnerability detection, yet existing approaches suffer from a fundamental precision-scalability tradeoff. Sound static analysis typically produces excessive false positives, while precise dynamic analysis fails to achieve comprehensive coverage. This paper presents a Multi-Granular Taint Propagation Framework (MGTPF) that significantly advances taint analysis theory through novel adaptive abstraction mechanisms. Our approach introduces context-sensitive taint propagation rules that dynamically adjust abstraction granularity based on program context sensitivity patterns. We formalize a hierarchy of abstraction levels and establish theoretical conditions for safe level transitions during analysis. The framework extends traditional taint domains with precision-sensitive tracking that enables selective refinement only where necessary for distinguishing genuine vulnerabilities from spurious flows. We prove that MGTPF maintains soundness while achieving substantial precision improvements through targeted refinement strategies. Experimental evaluation on benchmark programs demonstrates 68% reduction in false positives compared to state-of-the-art taint analyzers while maintaining reasonable computational overhead. This work provides a principled improvement to taint analysis theory that addresses the fundamental tension between precision and scalability in security-sensitive program analysis.

Automated debugging remains bottlenecked by rule-based approaches that lack semantic understanding of code behavior. This paper presents NeuralDebug, a paradigm-shifting automated debugging system that leverages large language models trained on millions of code changes to jointly detect, localize, and explain bugs. The system introduces a novel neural architecture that encodes program structure and semantic context to identify anomalous patterns indicative of defects. Unlike traditional tools relying on predefined bug patterns, NeuralDebug learns contextual bug manifestations from diverse software repositories, enabling generalization to novel defect types. The system provides interpretable explanations by generating natural language descriptions of bug causes and potential fixes. We designed an efficient inference pipeline that achieves industrial applicability with average response times under two seconds for codebases exceeding one million lines. NeuralDebug was evaluated on comprehensive benchmarks including BugsInPy and Defects4J, achieving 94.2% precision and 89.7% recall, representing a 23% improvement in F1 score over state-of-the-art automated debugging tools. This work represents a paradigm shift from pattern-matching approaches toward semantic understanding of software defects through deep learning.

Mutation testing represents the gold standard for test suite quality assessment, yet current tools fail to scale beyond small codebases due to exponential growth in generated mutants. This paper presents TestForge, a high-performance mutation testing framework that significantly advances scalability through intelligent mutant management and distributed execution. TestForge introduces a novel mutant clustering algorithm that groups semantically equivalent mutants to eliminate redundant executions, achieving an order-of-magnitude reduction in testing workload without compromising assessment accuracy. The system implements a priority-based scheduling mechanism that prioritizes computationally expensive mutants likely to reveal test weaknesses. We designed an adaptive parallelization strategy that dynamically allocates computational resources based on detected mutation patterns and test characteristics. TestForge achieves 92% correlation with exhaustive mutation testing while reducing execution time from days to approximately four hours for large-scale industrial systems. The framework was validated on fifteen open-source projects totaling 2.3 million lines of code and integrated with continuous integration pipelines without introducing unacceptable latency. This work provides a practical solution for mutation testing adoption in modern software development, significantly improving test quality assessment for industrial-scale systems.
